title: X Feed Digest
summary: GPT-5.2 updates are rolling into ChatGPT and now power Deep Research, signaling steady model improvements in core workflows.
Claude broadened access to workflow features (files, connectors, skills) while the MCP ecosystem gains new integrations like Excalidraw.
Enterprise AI coding adoption is scaling fast—Codex is rolling out across NVIDIA—while compute investment accelerates with xAI’s giant GPU buildout.
Open-weight models are closing the gap (GLM-5 leads benchmarks), and AI business momentum shows up in revenues like Databricks’ $5.4B run rate.

items.title: @OpenAI: Deep Research now on GPT-5.2
items.body: OpenAI says ChatGPT’s Deep Research mode is now powered by GPT‑5.2 and is rolling out with more improvements to come. It’s a signal that model upgrades are landing first in research workflows.

items.title: @claudeai: Free plan gets files + connectors
items.body: Anthropic is expanding Claude’s free tier to include file creation, connectors, and skills—features that previously required a subscription. This widens access to practical workflow tools.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex rolling out at NVIDIA
items.body: OpenAI says Codex is being deployed company‑wide at NVIDIA to roughly 30k engineers, with enterprise controls like US‑only processing and admin guardrails. A strong signal of large‑scale agent adoption.

items.title: @excalidraw: Official MCP for Claude
items.body: Excalidraw announced an official MCP integration with Claude, available via Connectors and Claude Code. This makes diagram creation and editing a first‑class tool inside Claude workflows.

items.title: @demishassabis: Isomorphic drug design SOTA
items.body: Demis Hassabis reports Isomorphic Labs’ drug‑design engine is pushing state‑of‑the‑art accuracy on key benchmarks for in‑silico discovery. It’s another signal of AI’s growing impact in biotech.

items.title: @ArtificialAnlys: GLM‑5 leads open‑weights
items.body: Artificial Analysis says Z.ai’s GLM‑5 now tops their open‑weights Intelligence Index, with big gains in agentic tasks and reduced hallucination. The report positions it closer to proprietary frontier models.

items.title: @thenextweb: Databricks at $5.4B run rate
items.body: Databricks reportedly reached a $5.4B revenue run rate and a $134B valuation, with about $1.4B tied to AI products. The update suggests real enterprise AI spend is materializing in revenue.

items.title: @SawyerMerritt: xAI’s giant GPU buildout
items.body: A summary of xAI’s new supercomputer claims 330k+ GPUs and over 1GW of power in phase one, with another 220k GPUs planned. If accurate, it highlights the accelerating scale of AI compute capex.

items.title: @ivalong_com: AI video shocks Unity
items.body: Commentary notes Unity’s shares fell sharply after a surge of AI‑generated content (“即梦”), arguing the market is repricing traditional content tools. It’s a reminder of how quickly AI‑native workflows can pressure incumbents.

items.title: @tesla_na: Model 3/Y under $40k
items.body: Tesla‑focused account says Model 3 and Model Y now start below $40k and include supervised self‑driving. Pricing moves like this continue to shape EV demand and margins.

items.title: @immersivetran: The productivity power of “No”
items.body: A recap of James Clear’s point that real productivity comes from saying no up front, not optimizing endless commitments. The framing: “No” preserves time for the few things that truly matter.

items.title: @immersivetran: Digital minimalism toolkit
items.body: A curated “digital minimalism” toolkit suggests using tech to fight attention‑draining apps—grayscale launchers, feed blockers, forced breaks, and RSS cleanup. The idea is to engineer the environment, not rely on willpower.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Leverage beats raw talent
items.body: This thread argues outcomes hinge on leverage and distribution more than raw intelligence—smart people without reach stay capped, while platforms scale impact exponentially. It’s a useful lens for career and product strategy.
